name: Abiram
source_summary: A Reubenite who, with his brother Dathan and Korah the Levite, led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron's God-given authority in the wilderness; when he defiantly refused Moses' summons, the ground opened and swallowed him, his family, and his co-conspirators alive.
family_friendly_summary: Abiram was one of the leaders of a rebellion against Moses and Aaron while Israel was traveling through the wilderness. Along with his brother Dathan and a man named Korah, Abiram gathered followers who complained that Moses had too much authority. When Moses called Abiram and Dathan to come talk with him, they refused and spoke to him with contempt. Moses warned everyone to step back from the rebels' tents, and then something astonishing happened: the ground split open and swallowed Abiram, his family, and his fellow rebels. It was a frightening reminder that God had chosen Moses and Aaron to lead His people, and rejecting that leadership meant rejecting God Himself.
adult_story: Abiram, a Reubenite, joined his brother Dathan and 250 leading Israelites, together with Korah of the tribe of Levi, in open rebellion against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness, charging, "You have gone far enough, for all the congregation are holy... Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?" (Numbers 16:1-3). When Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram to answer for their rebellion, they refused outright, accusing Moses of failing to bring Israel into the promised land and of trying to lord it over them (16:12-14). Moses warned the whole community to separate from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, declaring that if the LORD did something entirely new -- if the ground itself opened and swallowed them alive -- the people would know these men had spurned the LORD (16:23-30). As soon as Moses finished speaking, the earth split open beneath them and swallowed Dathan, Abiram, their households, and all their possessions; fire also consumed the 250 who had offered incense with Korah (16:31-35). Numbers 26:9-10 and Deuteronomy 11:6 both recall the event as a warning to later generations, and Psalm 106:17 remembers it as a sign of God's judgment on rebellion against His appointed leadership.
devotionals: Abiram refused to follow the leaders God had chosen, and it led somewhere very sad. May we listen well to those God has placed over us.
Jesus is the leader God sent to care for us forever. May we follow him, rather than turn away the way Abiram did.
